title: Moving to Columbia TN: A Buyer Guide From Nashville or Away
description: Moving to Columbia TN from Nashville or out of state? Here is current Maury County market data, costs to plan for, and what to verify before you buy.
body:
If you are moving to Columbia TN, you are probably weighing a few things at once: price, commute, taxes and schools. This guide covers what the current data says, what changes when you cross county lines, and what to check before you make an offer.

Columbia is in Maury County, along the Duck River. It is not in Williamson County, so some of the rules and services you may know from Franklin or Brentwood will not carry over.

## What the Columbia numbers say right now

{{img:0}}

According to Redfin (rolling 3 months, data as of 2026-10-31), Columbia's median sale price was $354,753, down 1.4% from a year earlier. Median days on market was 75, and the average sale-to-list ratio was 96.8%. There were 450 active listings.

Redfin also shows 5.0 months of supply for Columbia. Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 is balanced, and over 6 favors buyers. At 5.0, Columbia sits in the balanced range.

Other sources add context. Zillow Research puts Columbia's Market Temperature Index at 32, which it reads as leaning toward buyers. That index is up 11 points over 3 months, so the trend is heating. Realtor.com Research shows Maury County hotness at 35.4 out of 100. These are snapshots, not predictions, and they can shift.

For comparison, Redfin's Nashville metro figures for the 4 weeks ending 2026-11-08 show a median sale price of $467,332, 69 median days on market, a 97.7% sale-to-list ratio and 5.9 months of supply across 2,232 homes sold. The two data sets cover different areas and time windows, so use them as context rather than a direct match.

Conditions also vary by price range and by street. For the wider corridor, see our [Market data for the I-65 corridor](/market-data).

## What changes on paper when you move from Nashville

**County and city.** Within Columbia, you deal with the [City of Columbia](https://www.columbiatn.gov) and [Maury County Government](https://www.maurycounty-tn.gov). If you are comparing nearby towns, note that Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties. County services, schools and taxes can differ by address there. See [City of Spring Hill](https://www.springhilltn.org) for that city's own information, or our [Columbia vs Spring Hill](/columbia/columbia-vs-spring-hill) page.

Murfreesboro is in Rutherford County. If it is also on your list, the City of Murfreesboro site is the place for local details.

**Property taxes.** For the 2025 tax year, inside Columbia city limits, the combined rate is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value. That is $1.91 for the county and $0.8251 for the city. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25% of appraised value. The source is the Maury County community profile for Columbia, which cites the Tennessee Comptroller, Division of Property Assessments.

Those are the latest 2025 rates I found. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, when rates are reset, so the 2026 rates may be lower. Your actual bill depends on the exact address, so confirm with the Maury County Trustee before you budget.

**Schools.** Columbia addresses are zoned through [Maury County Public Schools](https://www.mauryk12.org), the county district. Zoning depends on the exact address. The most reliable way to find the zoned school for a home is the district's own lookup tool. Our [Columbia school districts](/columbia/schools) page is a starting point, but verify with the district for any home you are serious about.

**Utilities and services.** Providers can differ from one address to the next. Confirm which providers serve the specific home you are considering before you plan your move-in.

## Commute and daily life

{{img:1}}

The U.S. Census Bureau (American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2020 to 2024) reports a mean travel time to work of 28 minutes for Columbia. That is an average across all workers, not a promise for any route or hour. If you plan to commute toward Nashville, test the drive at the times you would actually make it. [TDOT SmartWay traffic](https://smartway.tn.gov) shows current road conditions, and our [Columbia commute times](/columbia/commute) page is another place to start.

The same Census data lists a median household income of $63,719 and a median gross rent of $1,197 per month. It also shows 63.3% of homes are owner-occupied. Our [Columbia ZIP codes and Census numbers](/columbia/neighborhoods) page has more on the area's numbers.

## The full cost of buying, not just the price

Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs. Request quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies, and book early for month-end dates.

Freddie Mac, via FRED, reports the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week of 2026-11-12. Nobody can reliably predict where rates will go. Some buyers buy now and plan to refinance later, but refinancing is not guaranteed and has its own closing costs. Treat it as a possibility, not a plan.

A useful way to frame the decision is to compare the full monthly cost of buying (payment, taxes, insurance, maintenance) with the monthly cost of renting a comparable home, and to weigh how long you expect to stay. Try your own figures in the [Mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator), and see [Columbia cost of living](/columbia/cost-of-living) for more budget context.

Buyers can also ask about negotiating, such as asking the seller to pay some closing costs or fund an interest rate buydown. Whether that is available depends on the seller, the home and the market, and your lender must confirm what is allowed for your loan.

## If you are buying from out of state

A few steps matter more when you cannot walk through the house on short notice:

- **Get pre-approved, not just pre-qualified.** Pre-approval means a lender has reviewed your documents. It is not a final loan commitment, since final approval depends on the appraisal, underwriting and your finances staying the same until closing.
- **Compare Loan Estimates.** The CFPB encourages getting estimates from more than one lender. You choose your own lender.
- **Plan inspections.** Radon testing, a sewer scope and a termite inspection are common add-ons to a standard home inspection. Termite and wood-destroying organism inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee.
- **Read the disclosures.** Tennessee sellers complete the residential property condition disclosure (or exemption). The lead-based paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.
- **Watch for wire fraud.** Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust. Never rely on emailed instructions.
- **Check water and flood questions by address.** If a home is near the Duck River or any other water, ask about flood maps and insurance for that specific address.

From the time you apply for a loan through closing, avoid opening new credit, financing furniture or changing jobs. Cancel homeowner's insurance on a sold home only after closing is confirmed. Our [Free moving checklists](/checklists) can help keep the move organized.

## Next steps

If you want local help sorting through Columbia and Maury County, the simplest step is to fill out the form at [Get matched with homes](/buy#form). Scott will schedule a call, and you will be talking within the next 48 hours. If you would rather ask a question first, use [Contact Scott](/contact). You can also read the [Columbia real estate guide](/columbia) on your own time.

faq.q: Is Columbia, TN in Williamson County?
faq.a: No. Columbia is in Maury County. Murfreesboro is in Rutherford County, and Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties.

faq.q: What is the property tax rate in Columbia, TN?
faq.a: For the 2025 tax year inside Columbia city limits, the combined rate is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value, with residential property assessed at 25% of appraised value. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, so confirm current rates with the Maury County Trustee.

faq.q: Which school district serves Columbia, TN homes?
faq.a: Columbia addresses are zoned through Maury County Public Schools. Zoning depends on the exact address, so use the district's own lookup tool to verify any home.

faq.q: Is Columbia a buyer's market right now?
faq.a: Redfin shows 5.0 months of supply for Columbia as of 2026-10-31, which falls in the balanced range of 4 to 6 months. Zillow's Market Temperature Index of 32 reads as leaning toward buyers, and conditions vary by price range and address.
